value.answer: This sounds like classic teething - drooling, gnawing on things, and extra fussiness are all typical when new teeth are coming in. A cool teething ring, a clean cold cloth to chew on, or gentle gum rubbing usually helps. Teething alone shouldn't cause high fever, vomiting, or diarrhea - if those show up, something else may be going on.
value.triage: If fussiness is mild and your toddler is eating, drinking, and otherwise acting normal, watching at home is reasonable - call 811 if fussiness is severe, feeding drops off, or you're unsure what's going on. Go to the ER or call 911 if there's high fever, trouble breathing, a rash that doesn't fade with pressure, or your child seems very unwell or hard to wake.
